docs.title: SpliceVI
docs.text: SpliceVI is a multimodal variational autoencoder that jointly models gene expression and alternative splicing (junction usage / PSI) from single-cell data. It learns a joint low-dimensional representation of cells from both modalities, imputes junction usage, and tests for differential splicing and expression between groups of cells. In sparse atlases it can find splicing differences that pseudobulk tests have too few reads to assess.

docs.title: Ecosystem overview
docs.text:
SpliceVI and LeafletFA read the same splicing format, SplicingDataset, which ATSEmapper builds from junction reads.

flowchart TD
    A[BAM files per cell] --> B[regtools junction extract]
    B --> C[ATSEmapper]
    C --> D["SplicingDataset.h5ad\ncell_by_junction_matrix\ncell_by_cluster_matrix"]
    D --> E[LeafletFA]
    D --> F[SpliceVI]
    E --> G["Splicing Programs (K factors)\nCell SP activities"]
    F --> H["Joint latent space\nDifferential analysis"]
Tool Role Repo Docs ATSEmapper BAM files → SplicingDataset daklab/ATSEmapper LeafletFA Beta-Dirichlet factor model for splicing programs daklab/LeafletFA docs SpliceVI Multimodal VAE (splicing + gene expression) daklab/SpliceVI this site

ATSEmapper groups the junctions found by regtools into ATSEs and writes the read counts in this format.

docs.title: Quick install
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/daklab/SpliceVI.git
cd SpliceVI
pip install -e .

docs.title: Minimal example
docs.text:
import mudata
from splicevi import SPLICEVI

mdata = mudata.read_h5mu("train_data.h5mu")

SPLICEVI.setup_mudata(mdata, batch_key="mouse.id")   # layer names default to the expected layout

model = SPLICEVI(mdata)   # defaults = the paper's settings
model.train()

latent = model.get_latent_representation()   # (cells × n_latent) joint latent space
psi    = model.get_normalized_splicing_DM()  # (cells × junctions) imputed PSI values

See SpliceVI model for the full parameter reference and SpliceVI MuData Object for the expected input structure.

docs.title: SpliceVI MuData Object
docs.text: SpliceVI takes a MuData object as input, with two modalities keyed "rna" and "splicing". This page describes the required structure of each modality and how the MuData is assembled from raw inputs.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
MuData
├── mdata["rna"]       AnnData   (cells × genes)       gene expression
└── mdata["splicing"]  AnnData   (cells × junctions)   splicing

Both modalities share the same obs (cell barcodes / metadata) index. All cells must be present in both modalities.

docs.title: RNA modality (mdata["rna"])
docs.text: Slot Contents .X Raw gene expression counts (cells × genes), integer dtype .layers["length_norm"] Length-normalized expression (raw counts divided by transcript length and rescaled to the median transcript length across genes), used as the model's expression input .var["gene_id"] Ensembl gene ID .var["modality"] "Gene_Expression" .obsm["X_library_size"] Per-cell library size (sum of length-normalized counts), shape (cells, 1)

docs.title: Length normalization
docs.text:
The length_norm layer is computed as follows.

length_norm = (raw_counts / transcript_length) × median(transcript_length across all genes)

This corrects for transcript length while keeping values on a count-like scale for the count likelihood (zero-inflated negative binomial by default).

docs.title: Splicing modality (mdata["splicing"])
docs.text:
The splicing AnnData follows the SplicingDataset format defined by LeafletFA. It needs these two layers of read counts.

Layer Shape Contents cell_by_junction_matrix cells × junctions Integer junction read counts (sparse) cell_by_cluster_matrix cells × junctions Total read counts across all junctions in the same ATSE (sparse), the denominator of PSI

Two more layers are computed from them when the MuData is assembled.

Layer Shape Contents junc_ratio cells × junctions PSI values, junction_counts / atse_total_counts, or 0 where unobserved psi_mask cells × junctions Binary mask, 1 where atse_total_counts > 0 (the junction is observed in that cell) and 0 otherwise

docs.title: What is an ATSE?
docs.text: An alternative transcript structure event (ATSE) is a group of junctions in a gene that compete at shared splice sites. Two junctions belong to the same ATSE if they share a donor or an acceptor site (connected through other junctions of the ATSE). A cassette exon, for example, is one ATSE with a skipping junction and two inclusion junctions. Junctions that share no splice site with another junction are not part of any ATSE. All junctions of the same ATSE share the same cell_by_cluster_matrix value within a cell, and the model's junction usages within an ATSE sum to 1.

docs.title: PSI mask
docs.text: The psi_mask tells the model which values are observed. SpliceVI's partial encoder processes only observed junctions (mask = 1) in each cell and ignores positions where psi_mask = 0, and the splicing likelihood is evaluated on observed ATSEs only. Unobserved junctions are therefore treated as missing, not as zero usage.

docs.title: var metadata
docs.text: Column Contents junction_id Unique junction identifier, chrom_start_end_strand (e.g. chr1_52199887_52207300_-) event_id ATSE identifier (shared by all junctions of the same ATSE) modality "Splicing"

docs.title: Shared obs metadata
docs.text:
mdata.obs is the union of obs columns from both modalities. Typical columns are listed below.

Column Description cell_type / broad_cell_type Cell type annotation tissue Tissue of origin age / age_numeric Age (string or parsed integer) mouse.id / donor_id Batch/donor identifier used for batch correction

docs.title: Data format
docs.text:
SpliceVI expects a MuData object with two modalities that hold the same cells:

  • rna holds gene expression (cells × genes). The model reads layers["length_norm"], and the library size of each cell is in mdata.obsm["X_library_size"].
  • splicing holds the junctions (cells × junctions), with these layers:
    • cell_by_junction_matrix, the reads of each junction
    • cell_by_cluster_matrix, the reads of the junction's ATSE, repeated for each junction of the ATSE
    • junc_ratio, the junction usage (PSI), which is junction reads / ATSE reads and 0 where the ATSE has no reads
    • psi_mask, which is 1 where the ATSE has reads in the cell and 0 otherwise

Its var["event_id"] gives the ATSE each junction belongs to.

These are the default names of SPLICEVI.setup_mudata, and other names can be passed to it. The SpliceVI MuData Object page describes every field. See the SplicingDataset documentation in LeafletFA for utilities to construct this format from raw data.

docs.title: Using the Python API
docs.text:
import mudata
from splicevi import SPLICEVI

mdata = mudata.read_h5mu("train_data.h5mu")

# Layer and modality names default to the layout in "SpliceVI MuData Object";
# pass e.g. rna_layer="raw_counts" if your expression counts are in another layer.
SPLICEVI.setup_mudata(mdata, batch_key="mouse.id")

# The defaults are the paper's model and training settings.
model = SPLICEVI(mdata)
model.train()

model.save("models/my_run/")

docs.title: Using the SLURM script
docs.text:
train_splicevi.py trains one model from a MuData file. Every argument of SPLICEVI(...) and train() is also a command-line flag, and flags left out keep the paper defaults.

python train_splicevi.py --train_mdata_path train_data.h5mu --model_dir models/my_run --batch_key mouse.id --seed 1
python train_splicevi.py --help     # all flags with their defaults

train_splicevi.sh runs the same command as a SLURM job. Set the data path, output folder and batch key at its top (other settings go in its EXTRA_ARGS line, for example EXTRA_ARGS="--max_epochs 100 --lr 5e-4") and submit it.

mkdir -p logs && sbatch train_splicevi.sh

docs.title: Extracting outputs
docs.text:
model = SPLICEVI.load("models/my_run/", adata=mdata)

# Joint latent representation
latent = model.get_latent_representation()          # (cells × n_latent)

# Modality-specific latents
z_expr = model.get_latent_representation(modality="expression")
z_spl  = model.get_latent_representation(modality="splicing")

# Imputed PSI values: posterior mean junction usage given each cell's reads
psi = model.get_normalized_splicing_DM()            # (cells × junctions)

docs.title: splicevi.splicevae.SPLICEVAE
docs.text:
Bases: BaseModuleClass

Variational auto encoder for joint (paired or unpaired) RNA-seq gene expression and alternative splicing (junction usage). Two encoder–decoder branches (expression and splicing) produce posterior latents that are mixed into a shared latent space z.

Reconstruction is performed per modality. Optional penalties align the two posteriors.

The defaults are the settings of the paper's models (the same as :class:SPLICEVI's defaults). The model class always passes every setting explicitly, so these defaults only matter when the module is built directly.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default n_input_genes int

Number of gene expression features (G).

0 n_input_junctions int

Number of splicing junction features (J).

0 n_batch int

Number of batches for batch correction (categorical covariate).

0 n_obs int

Number of observations (cells); needed when modality_weights="cell".

0 n_labels int

Number of labels (for gene_dispersion="gene-label").

0 n_cats_per_cov Iterable[int] or None

Category counts for each categorical covariate provided.

None n_continuous_cov int

Number of continuous covariates.

0 gene_likelihood (zinb, nb, poisson)

Expression likelihood.

"zinb","nb","poisson" gene_dispersion (gene, gene - batch, gene - label, gene - cell)

Dispersion layout for expression.

"gene","gene-batch","gene-label","gene-cell" use_size_factor_key bool

If True, use provided library size factors for expression. Otherwise learn a library size encoder.

False splicing_encoder_architecture (vanilla, partial)

Splicing encoder choice: "vanilla" uses a standard SCVI Encoder. "partial" uses PartialEncoderEDDIFaster.

"vanilla","partial" splicing_decoder_architecture (vanilla, linear)

Splicing decoder choice: "vanilla" uses DecoderSplice (nonlinear). "linear" uses a LinearDecoder.

"vanilla","linear" expression_architecture (vanilla, linear)

Expression decoder: "vanilla" uses a non linear DecoderSCVI. "linear" uses a LinearDecoderSCVI.

"vanilla","linear" n_hidden int or None

Hidden width for SCVI style MLPs. If None, defaults to roughly sqrt(J) capped at 128.

None n_latent int or None

Latent dimensionality. If None, roughly sqrt(n_hidden). When modality_weights="concatenate", the mixed latent is doubled internally.

30 n_layers_encoder int

Depth of SCVI encoders (expression branch and splicing branch when splicing_encoder_architecture="vanilla"). Also controls the depth of the post pooling MLP in the partial splicing encoder.

2 n_layers_decoder int

Depth of non linear decoders (expression "vanilla", splicing "vanilla"). Not used by linear decoders.

2 dropout_rate float

Dropout for SCVI style MLPs.

0.01 use_batch_norm (encoder, decoder, none, both)

Apply BatchNorm to encoder or decoder stacks.

"encoder","decoder","none","both" use_layer_norm (encoder, decoder, none, both)

Apply LayerNorm to encoder or decoder stacks.

"encoder","decoder","none","both" latent_distribution (normal, ln)

Posterior family for encoders. If "ln" (logistic normal), the latent sample is softmax transformed before decoding.

"normal","ln" deeply_inject_covariates bool

Deeply inject categorical and continuous covariates into decoder layers.

False encode_covariates bool

Concatenate continuous covariates to encoder inputs and pass categorical covariates via n_cat_list.

False splicing_loss_type (binomial, beta_binomial, dirichlet_multinomial)

Reconstruction loss for splicing. "binomial" expects junction counts and ATSE totals. "beta_binomial" uses a beta binomial with a learned concentration. "dirichlet_multinomial" uses grouped softmax within ATSEs.

"binomial","beta_binomial","dirichlet_multinomial" dm_concentration (atse, scalar)

For Dirichlet multinomial. Controls whether the concentration is per ATSE or scalar.

"atse","scalar" splicing_loss_weight float

Scalar multiplier applied to the splicing reconstruction loss before it is combined with the expression reconstruction loss. Values > 1 upweight splicing relative to expression; values < 1 downweight it.

1.0 lambda_prior float

Weight of the L2 penalty (torch.square(log_phi_j).sum()) pulling the learned per-ATSE (or scalar) log-concentration toward 0, added to the loss whenever splicing_loss_type is "beta_binomial" or "dirichlet_multinomial". This shrinks log_phi_j away from wherever it's initialized (not toward the init value) -- ATSEs with weak/sparse reconstruction-loss gradient collapse toward this prior's fixed point (log_phi_j=0, i.e. phi=softplus(0)~=0.69) while ATSEs with strong data support resist it. Higher values shrink more aggressively; 0.0 disables it. Only used when phi_prior="l2_log".

1e-2 phi_floor float

Minimum concentration: phi = phi_floor + softplus(log_phi_j). Additive so the gradient stays smooth (a clamp would kill it below the floor). 0.0 = no floor.

0.0 phi_prior (l2_log, gamma, none)

Regularizer on the concentration. "l2_log" is an L2 pull of log_phi_j toward 0 (weight lambda_prior, divided by batch size). "gamma" is a MAP Gamma(phi_prior_shape, phi_prior_rate) prior on the effective phi, scaled by 1/n_obs (proper MAP scaling for a per-cell-mean loss). "none" disables it.

"l2_log","gamma","none" psi_prior_pseudocount float

Pseudo-count prior on the decoded PSI (dirichlet_multinomial only): adds -psi_prior_pseudocount * sum_j pi_j log p_j per cell, i.e. that many virtual reads per ATSE distributed as the population PSI pi (buffer psi_prior_pop, filled by the model class). Entries without reads are pulled to the population PSI; entries with reads are dominated by their data. 0 = off.

0.0 phi_prior_shape float, defaults 2.0, 0.1

Gamma prior parameters (rate parametrization; defaults give mean 20, sd ~14).

2.0 phi_prior_rate float, defaults 2.0, 0.1

Gamma prior parameters (rate parametrization; defaults give mean 20, sd ~14).

2.0 phi_init (constant, log100, prior)

"constant" starts every raw log_phi_j at exactly log 100 (phi ~ 4.6 after softplus). "log100" adds a random draw to that start (raw log_phi_j ~ N(log 100, 0.5)); the per-ATSE concentration is not identified from the data, so the draw only adds variance between replicates. "prior" samples phi from the Gamma prior (clamped above the floor) and inverts softplus.

"constant","log100","prior" code_dim int

Dimensionality of per junction codes before pooling.

64 h_hidden_dim int

Hidden width of the per junction h subnetwork that combines PSI and feature embedding.

128 encoder_hidden_dim int

Hidden width of the post pooling MLP that maps the pooled code to (mu, log var) of z.

128 pool_mode (mean, sum)

Aggregation of per junction codes within each cell.

"mean","sum" psi_input (deviation, raw)

Input of the partial splicing encoder. "deviation": each observed junction's PSI minus its read-weighted population PSI (buffer pop_psi, filled by the model class), the per-junction network's output at zero deviation is subtracted, and the pool is divided by a fixed number (the median number of observed junctions per training cell, buffer pool_divisor), so the pooled code does not carry the number of observed junctions. Needs pool_mode="mean". "raw": the observed PSI itself, averaged over the observed junctions.

"deviation","raw" decoder_depth_covariates bool

Give both decoders (never the encoders) three standardized depth inputs per cell: log1p detected genes, log1p observed junctions and log1p library size (standardized with the training data's mean and standard deviation, buffers depth_cov_mean / depth_cov_std). Vanilla splicing decoder only.

True max_nobs int

Optional cap on the number of observed entries processed in each scatter chunk. A negative value disables chunking.

-1 n_decoder_covariates int

Number of decoder covariate inputs (e.g. 1 for technology: 0 = reference data, 1 = query data). Each adds zero-initialized weights to the first hidden layer of both decoders (decoder_covariate_weight_expression and decoder_covariate_weight_splicing, one column per covariate), so at zero weights the model is unchanged. The value used for every cell is the buffer decoder_covariate_value unless decoder_covariate_batch (one row per cell) is set, as during :meth:SPLICEVI.finetune_decoders. Added after training by :meth:add_decoder_covariates; 0 = no covariate inputs. Vanilla decoders only.

0 modality_weights (equal, cell, universal, concatenate, per_dimension_weighted_average)

How to combine expression and splicing posteriors. "per_dimension_weighted_average" learns a per-latent-dimension splicing contribution weight w_d in [0,1] (expression weight = 1-w_d), constrained so the mean weight stays at 0.5 (preventing one modality from dominating globally).

"equal","cell","universal","concatenate","per_dimension_weighted_average" modality_penalty (Jeffreys, MMD, None)

Alignment penalty between the two posteriors on paired cells.

"Jeffreys","MMD","None" mask_cells_without_splicing bool

If True, a cell with no observed junction (psi_observed_mask all 0) is treated as lacking the splicing modality: it gets no splicing weight in the latent mix and is excluded from the modality-alignment penalty. If False (default) every cell always counts as having splicing, so a cell with no splicing reads still has its (uninformed) splicing posterior averaged into the joint latent.

False variance_mixing (sqrt_weights, linear, squared)

How the two encoders' variances are combined into the joint posterior variance for modality_weights in {"equal","cell","universal","per_dimension_weighted_average"} (ignored for "concatenate"). The mean is always the weighted average of means. "sqrt_weights": for equal/cell/universal the MultiVI heuristic sum(sqrt(w) * v) (~1.41x the average variance under equal weights); for per_dimension_weighted_average the rule (sum(w * std))2, the variance of an average of perfectly correlated errors. "linear" uses sum(w * v) (no inflation). "squared" uses sum(w2 * v), the variance of a weighted average of independent Gaussians (per-dimension w in the per-dimension mode); the default.

"sqrt_weights","linear","squared" **model_kwargs

Forwarded to underlying components.

{} Notes

The partial splicing branch uses a single PartialEncoderEDDIFaster encoder that aggregates only observed junctions per cell. The same n_layers_encoder parameter controls the depth of the final MLP that produces latent statistics for this branch.

docs.title: add_decoder_covariates(n_covariates=1)
docs.text:
Add n_covariates zero-initialized covariate inputs to the first hidden layer of both decoders.

Same as appending the covariates to each decoder's input: the first layer's output gets covariates @ W.T with W = decoder_covariate_weight_<decoder> (hidden units x covariates), initialized at zero so the model's output is unchanged until W is trained. The value fed for every cell is decoder_covariate_value (buffer, saved with the model; zeros = reference data) unless decoder_covariate_batch holds one row per cell.

docs.title: init_log_phi(size)
docs.text:
Initial raw concentration parameter. size=None gives the scalar DM parameter.

"constant" (default): every value starts at log 100 (phi = softplus(log 100), about 4.6). "log100": the same start plus a random draw (per-ATSE / per-junction: N(log 100, 0.5); scalar: 4.6). "prior" samples phi from the Gamma prior, clamps it above the floor, and inverts softplus so get_phi() starts at that sample.

docs.title: loss(tensors, inference_outputs, generative_outputs, kl_weight=1.0)
docs.text:
Compute the total loss combining gene expression and splicing reconstruction losses, latent KL divergence, and the modality alignment penalty.

For splicing, if count data is provided (via the keys "atse_counts_key" and "junc_counts_key"), the loss is computed using the specified binomial, DM, or beta-binomial likelihood; otherwise, binary cross-entropy is used.

Returns:

Type Description LossOutput

A container with total loss, reconstruction losses, and KL divergence details.

docs.title: splicevi.SPLICEVI
docs.text:
Bases: VAEMixin, UnsupervisedTrainingMixin, BaseModelClass, ArchesMixin

Joint model of gene expression and alternative splicing (junction usage) in single cells.

SPLICEVI learns one latent space from both modalities: an expression encoder and a splicing encoder each give a posterior over the latent space, the two are mixed into a joint posterior, and one decoder per modality reconstructs the data (zero-inflated negative binomial for expression, Dirichlet-multinomial over the junctions of each ATSE for splicing). It wraps the :class:~splicevi.splicevae.SPLICEVAE module.

The defaults are the settings of the paper's models, so SPLICEVI(mdata) followed by model.train() trains the paper's model. :meth:preset returns the same settings as dictionaries, with the variants for a batch key (atlas="tms") and for a reference plus a sparse atlas ("sparse", joint=True).

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default adata AnnOrMuData

MuData object with the modalities "rna" and "splicing", registered with :meth:setup_mudata.

required n_genes int | None

Number of genes. Taken from the registered data when left as None.

None n_junctions int | None

Number of junctions. Taken from the registered data when left as None.

None modality_weights Literal['equal', 'cell', 'universal', 'concatenate', 'per_dimension_weighted_average']

How the two posteriors are mixed into the joint latent:

  • "equal" (default): equal weight per modality,
  • "universal": one learned weight per modality,
  • "cell": learned weights per cell,
  • "concatenate": no mixing; the two latents are concatenated,
  • "per_dimension_weighted_average": one learned splicing weight per latent dimension (expression weight = 1 - splicing weight), constrained so that the mean weight stays at 0.5.
'equal' modality_penalty Literal['Jeffreys', 'MMD', 'None']

Penalty that aligns the two posteriors: "None" (default), "Jeffreys" or "MMD".

'None' n_hidden int | None

Width of the hidden layers of the encoders and decoders. If None (default), the square root of the number of junctions, capped at 128.

None n_latent int | None

Dimension of the latent space (of each modality's latent before concatenation). Default 30. If None, the square root of n_hidden.

30 n_layers_encoder int

Hidden layers in the encoders, including the network after pooling in the partial splicing encoder. Default 2.

2 n_layers_decoder int

Hidden layers in the decoders (not used by the linear decoders). Default 2.

2 dropout_rate float

Dropout rate in the hidden layers. Default 0.01.

0.01 use_batch_norm Literal['encoder', 'decoder', 'none', 'both']

Where to apply batch normalization: "encoder", "decoder", "both" or "none" (default).

'none' use_layer_norm Literal['encoder', 'decoder', 'none', 'both']

Where to apply layer normalization: "encoder", "decoder", "both" (default) or "none".

'both' latent_distribution Literal['normal', 'ln']

Latent distribution: "normal" (default) or "ln" (logistic normal).

'normal' deeply_inject_covariates bool

If True, covariates enter every decoder layer. Default False.

False encode_covariates bool

If True, covariates are also given to the encoders. Default False.

False gene_likelihood Literal['zinb', 'nb', 'poisson']

Expression likelihood: "zinb" (default), "nb" or "poisson".

'zinb' dispersion Literal['gene', 'gene-batch', 'gene-label', 'gene-cell']

Expression dispersion: "gene" (default), "gene-batch", "gene-label" or "gene-cell".

'gene' fully_paired bool

If True, the model exposes only the joint latent (no latent per modality). Default False.

False **model_kwargs

Passed on to :class:~splicevi.splicevae.SPLICEVAE.

{}

Other Parameters:

Name Type Description variance_mixing Literal['sqrt_weights', 'linear', 'squared']

How the two encoders' variances are combined into the joint posterior variance (every modality_weights except "concatenate"; the joint mean is always the weighted average of the two means):

  • "squared" (default): sum(w**2 * v), the variance of a weighted average of independent Gaussians,
  • "sqrt_weights": for equal/cell/universal weights the MultiVI rule sum(sqrt(w) * v) (about 1.41 times the average variance under equal weights); for per_dimension_weighted_average (sum(w * std))**2,
  • "linear": sum(w * v).
mask_cells_without_splicing bool

If True, cells with no observed junction get no splicing weight in the joint latent and are left out of the alignment penalty. Default False: every cell counts as having splicing.

splicing_loss_type Literal['binomial', 'beta_binomial', 'dirichlet_multinomial']

Splicing likelihood: "dirichlet_multinomial" (default), "beta_binomial" or "binomial".

dm_concentration Literal['atse', 'scalar']

Dirichlet-multinomial concentration: "atse" (default; one learned concentration per ATSE) or "scalar" (one shared value).

splicing_loss_weight float

Multiplier of the splicing reconstruction loss relative to the expression reconstruction loss. Default 1.0.

lambda_prior float

Weight of the L2 penalty that pulls each learned log-concentration toward 0 (phi_prior="l2_log" only). Default 0.01; 0.0 turns it off.

phi_floor float

Minimum concentration: phi = phi_floor + softplus(log_phi). Default 0.0.

phi_prior Literal['l2_log', 'gamma', 'none']

Regularizer on the concentration: "l2_log" (default; see lambda_prior), "gamma" (Gamma prior on phi with phi_prior_shape and phi_prior_rate, scaled by 1 / number of cells) or "none".

phi_prior_shape float

Shape and rate of the Gamma prior. Defaults 2.0 and 0.1 (mean 20).

phi_prior_rate float

Shape and rate of the Gamma prior. Defaults 2.0 and 0.1 (mean 20).

Starting concentration: "constant" (default; every ATSE starts at the same value, phi about 4.6), "log100" (the same start plus a random draw per ATSE) or "prior" (a draw from the Gamma prior).

Strength of the pseudo-count term on the decoded junction usage: adds -psi_prior_pseudocount * sum_j pop_psi_j * log(psi_j) per cell, i.e. that many virtual reads per ATSE distributed as the read-weighted population usage of the training data. Dirichlet-multinomial only. Default 0.0 (off).

Splicing encoder: "partial" (default; reads only the observed junctions of each cell) or "vanilla" (scvi-tools Encoder on the full junction vector).

Splicing decoder: "vanilla" (default; nonlinear) or "linear".

Expression decoder: "vanilla" (default; nonlinear) or "linear".

Width of the network after pooling in the partial splicing encoder. Default 128.

code_dim int

Size of the learned embedding of each junction in the partial splicing encoder. Default 64.

Width of the network that combines each observed junction's input with its embedding. Default 128.

Pooling over the observed junctions of a cell: "mean" (default) or "sum".

Input of the partial splicing encoder: "deviation" (default; each observed junction's usage minus its read-weighted population usage, pooled with a fixed divisor so the pooled code does not carry the number of observed junctions; needs pool_mode="mean") or "raw" (the observed usage itself).

Performs differential gene expression analysis using normalized gene expression estimates.

None group2 str | None

If it is a string, then it will query indices that verifies conditions on adata.obs, as described in :meth:pandas.DataFrame.query If idx1 is not None, this option overrides group1 and group2.

'change' delta float

specific case of region inducing differential expression. In this case, we suppose that :math:R \setminus [-\delta, \delta] does not induce differential expression (change model default case).

0.25 batch_size int | None

Minibatch size for data loading into model. Defaults to scvi.settings.batch_size.

None all_stats bool

Concatenate count statistics (e.g., mean expression group 1) to DE results.

True batch_correction bool

Whether to correct for batch effects in DE inference.

False batchid1 Iterable[str] | None

Subset of categories from batch_key registered in setup_anndata, e.g. ['batch1', 'batch2', 'batch3'], for group1. Only used if batch_correction is True, and by default all categories are used.

None batchid2 Iterable[str] | None

Same as batchid1 for group2. batchid2 must either have null intersection with batchid1, or be exactly equal to batchid1. When the two sets are exactly equal, cells are compared by decoding on the same batch. When sets have null intersection, cells from group1 and group2 are decoded on each group in group1 and group2, respectively.

None fdr_target float

Tag features as DE based on posterior expected false discovery rate.

0.05 silent bool

If True, disables the progress bar. Default: False.

False norm_expression_function Literal['decoder', 'zinb_expected', 'zinb_posterior_mean', 'zinb_posterior_sample']

Which expression estimate the two groups are compared on:

  • "zinb_expected" (default): the ZINB expected expression (1 - dropout) * px_scale. With ZINB the dropout probability can absorb part of a difference between groups, which px_scale alone then misses (on Allen Brain data downsampled to EasySci depth this roughly doubled the fold changes towards the full-depth ones). For a model with gene_likelihood="nb" or "poisson" there is no dropout, so this is the decoder output.
  • "decoder": the decoder output px_scale (:meth:get_normalized_expression), as in scVI and MultiVI.
  • "zinb_posterior_mean": the ZINB posterior mean given each cell's observed counts (:meth:get_normalized_expression_ZINB), which weighs in the raw data.

The two posterior options need gene_likelihood="zinb".

If given, scvi.settings.seed is set to this value before sampling, so that repeated calls give the same table. This seeds PyTorch, NumPy and Python's random for the whole session. Default None leaves the random state as it is.

None **kwargs

Additional keyword arguments for differential computation.

{}

Type Description A pandas DataFrame with differential expression results, sorted by ``proba_de`` (highest first). Features with equal ``proba_de`` keep their order in the data, and the FDR calls use the same order, so the table is the same on every machine.

docs.title: finetune_decoders(query_mdata, reference_mdata, n_query_per_step=32, n_reference_per_step=128, lr=0.0001, max_epochs=300, early_stopping_patience=30, validation_fraction=0.1, seed=20261137, set_torch_seed=True, max_minutes=None, checkpoint_dir=None, fix_depth_inputs=True, query_covariate_value=1.0, reference_covariate_value=0.0)
docs.text:
Adapt a trained model to a new atlas by fine-tuning only its decoders, plus one technology input.

Use when this model was trained on a reference atlas (e.g. Allen Brain, deep Smart-seq) and you want its expression and splicing estimates for a new, sparser atlas of the same tissue (e.g. EasySci, single-nucleus 3') without retraining from scratch. The encoders are not changed, so query cells are placed in the reference latent space; the decoders learn the query data's expression and splicing levels. Defaults are the same as what's used in the paper's EasySci model.

What happens:

  1. One zero-initialized decoder covariate input is added to the first hidden layer of both decoders (technology: reference_covariate_value for reference cells, query_covariate_value for query cells). At zero weights the model is the reference model.
  2. Everything is frozen except the two decoders and the covariate weights. Kept from the reference model: the encoders, junction embeddings and latent mixing, the deviation input's population PSI and pool divisor, the per-ATSE splicing concentrations and the gene dispersions (re-learning the last two on the query data predicted held-out query reads worse in the paper's tests, so it is not offered).
  3. With fix_depth_inputs (models with decoder_depth_covariates), the decoders' depth inputs are fixed at the reference training mean for every cell, since the reference depth statistics do not describe the query data. The cross-modality gate is set open, as at the end of training.
  4. Each step uses n_query_per_step query cells and n_reference_per_step reference cells (the reference "replay" keeps the decoders fitting the reference); loss = query loss + reference loss; Adam at lr.
  5. A random validation_fraction of the query cells is held out for early stopping (patience early_stopping_patience epochs, at most max_epochs, optional wall-clock limit max_minutes).
  6. The best state is restored and the model is left decoding as query data (decoder covariate = query_covariate_value), ready for :meth:differential_splicing etc. on the query cells.

Calling it again continues from the current weights with a fresh optimizer. Training a fine-tuned model with :meth:train is not supported: every cell would get decoder_covariate_value, so the covariate weights would act as a plain bias.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default query_mdata MuData

The new atlas (e.g. EasySci training metacells) in this model's gene and junction space (same genes, same junction ids and ATSE assignment), with the layers this model was trained on: expression counts (length_norm; raw counts for UMI data), library size (X_library_size), junction and ATSE counts, junc_ratio and psi_mask. If not yet set up, it is set up with this model's setup arguments (as :meth:load does). The paper's reproduction code (SpliceVI-utils) shows how these files were built from the model-ready data.

required reference_mdata MuData

A replay set of the data this model was trained on (e.g. 20,000 Allen training cells), same layers.

required n_query_per_step int

Query and reference cells per optimization step (paper: 32 and 128).

32 n_reference_per_step int

Query and reference cells per optimization step (paper: 32 and 128).

32 lr float

Adam learning rate.

0.0001 max_epochs int

Epochs over the query training cells; stop when the validation loss has not improved for this many epochs.

300 early_stopping_patience int

Epochs over the query training cells; stop when the validation loss has not improved for this many epochs.

300 validation_fraction float

Share of query cells held out (never trained on) to decide when to stop.

0.1 seed int

Seed of the validation split, the minibatch order and the reference cells per step (numpy), and, with set_torch_seed, of torch's global random state (latent sampling and decoder dropout during fine-tuning). GPU arithmetic is not bit-deterministic, so reruns agree closely but not exactly.

20261137 set_torch_seed bool

Call torch.manual_seed(seed) (changes torch's global random state). False when the caller seeded torch already, e.g. before loading the model, as the paper's fine-tuning run did.

True max_minutes float | None

Optional wall-clock limit (the best state so far is kept). Keep it below a job's time limit.

None checkpoint_dir str | None

If set, the best module state is also written to <checkpoint_dir>/module_state_best.pt at every improvement, so a run killed from outside (e.g. a job time limit) keeps its best state.

None fix_depth_inputs bool

Fix the decoders' depth inputs at the reference training mean (models with decoder depth covariates).

True query_covariate_value float

Values of the technology input for query and reference cells.

1.0 reference_covariate_value float

Values of the technology input for query and reference cells.

1.0

Returns:

Type Description Training history: one row per epoch (``epoch``, ``train_loss``, ``validation_loss``; epoch -1 = before training). Also stored as ``finetune_history_``, with the settings and outcome in ``finetune_params_``; both are saved by :meth:`save`.

Examples:

>>> model = SPLICEVI.load(reference_model_dir, adata=query_mdata)
>>> model.to_device("cuda")
>>> history = model.finetune_decoders(query_mdata, reference_mdata)
>>> model.save(out_dir)                         # SPLICEVI.load(out_dir, adata=query_mdata) decodes as query
>>> ds = model.differential_splicing(adata=query_mdata, groupby="broad_cell_type", group1="A", group2="B")

docs.text:
Returns ZINB posterior-mean normalized expression (the expression analogue of :meth:get_normalized_splicing_DM). Only valid for gene_likelihood="zinb".

The ZINB is a Gamma-Poisson mixed with a point mass at zero. With decoder mean :math:\mu (px_rate), inverse dispersion :math:\theta (px_r) and dropout probability :math:\pi = \sigma(\text{px\_dropout}), the posterior mean of the underlying rate given the observed count :math:y is

  • :math:y > 0: :math:E[\lambda \mid y] = \mu (\theta + y) / (\theta + \mu), i.e. a weighted average :math:\tfrac{\theta}{\theta+\mu}\mu + \tfrac{\mu}{\theta+\mu} y of the decoder and the data;
  • :math:y = 0: with :math:w = P(\text{dropout} \mid y=0) = \pi / (\pi + (1-\pi)(\theta/(\theta+\mu))^\theta), :math:E[\lambda \mid 0] = w \mu + (1-w)\, \theta\mu / (\theta+\mu) (a dropout zero carries no information; a sampling zero pulls the estimate down).

The result is divided by the cell's library factor (px_rate / px_scale), so it is on the same scale as :meth:get_normalized_expression (px_scale) and can replace it in DE. Parameters and return shape are the same as :meth:get_normalized_expression, plus:

sample If True, return one random draw from the posterior instead of its mean: for y > 0, :math:\lambda \sim \mathrm{Gamma}(\theta + y,\ \theta/\mu + 1); for y = 0, with probability w the prior :math:\mathrm{Gamma}(\theta, \theta/\mu) (dropout zero) and otherwise :math:\mathrm{Gamma}(\theta, \theta/\mu + 1) (Gamma shape / rate). Used by DE with norm_expression_function="zinb_posterior_sample", so each Monte Carlo draw carries the uncertainty of each cell's expression given its counts. return_counts If True, do not divide by the library factor (values on the count scale, e.g. for pseudobulk sums).

Returns DM-normalized splicing probabilities (PSI*).

This decodes junction PSI (:math:p) and applies a Dirichlet–multinomial posterior mean smoothing per junction: :math:\psi^\* = (c p + y_j) / (c + n), where :math:y_j is the observed junction count and :math:n is the observed ATSE total for that junction. The concentration :math:c is taken from the module: * If self.dm_concentration == "atse": use the per-ATSE values in self.module.log_phi_j mapped to per-junction via self.module.junc2atse. * Otherwise: treat self.module.log_phi_j as a scalar concentration.

Start the splicing decoder's per-junction bias at log(population PSI), clipped to [1e-4, 1].

With the hidden contribution at zero, the decoder then reproduces the population PSI: generative() maps sigmoid(bias) -> clamp -> logit -> softmax within the ATSE, which is the softmax of the bias over the ATSE.

Read-weighted population PSI per junction from the registered count layers of the training data.

Sum over cells of the junction counts divided by the sum over cells of the ATSE totals (the ATSE count layer repeats the ATSE total on every junction of the ATSE, so its column sum is the ATSE's read total); 0 for junctions without reads.

docs.title: SpliceVI
docs.text:
SpliceVI is a multimodal variational autoencoder that jointly models gene expression and alternative splicing (junction usage / PSI) from single-cell data. It learns a joint low-dimensional latent space from both modalities, which is used to impute junction usage and to test for differential splicing and expression.

SpliceVI follows the same overall architecture and inherits the same scvi-tools mixins as MultiVI (Ashuach et al., 2021), which jointly models RNA-seq and chromatin accessibility. The key difference is that the ATAC branch is replaced throughout by a splicing-specific branch, with a missingness-aware encoder, a splicing-specific decoder, and splicing likelihoods (Binomial / Beta-Binomial / Dirichlet-Multinomial) suited to the PSI scale. The DE/DS analysis API mirrors MultiVI's, with get_normalized_splicing and differential_splicing replacing the accessibility equivalents.

Ashuach T*, Gabitto MI*, Jordan MI, Yosef N. MultiVI: deep generative model for the integration of multi-modal data. bioRxiv, 2021.

docs.title: Model overview
docs.text:
SpliceVI uses two separate encoder branches, one for gene expression and one for splicing, whose posteriors are mixed into a joint latent space. Two decoder branches reconstruct each modality from the joint latent.

Gene expression ──► GE Encoder ──► q(z|x_e) ──┐
                                                ├──► Mix ──► z ──► GE Decoder ──► x_e
Splicing (PSI) ───► Splice Encoder ──► q(z|x_s) ─┘              └──► Splice Decoder ──► x_s

docs.title: Splicing encoder
docs.text:
Because splicing observations are highly sparse (many junctions are unobserved in a given cell), SpliceVI uses a missingness-aware partial encoder (PartialEncoderEDDIFaster). The design draws inspiration from the EDDI framework (Ma et al., 2019), which handles pervasive missing values in VAEs using feature embeddings and exchangeable neural networks (see also the SpliceVI preprint). The encoder works in three steps.

  1. Embeds each observed junction independently via a shared \(h\) network. By default (psi_input="deviation") the input is how much the junction's usage in the cell differs from its usage across all cells, so that which junctions are detected carries no signal on its own
  2. Pools the per-junction embeddings across all observed junctions in a cell (divided by a fixed number, the median number of observed junctions per training cell)
  3. Maps the pooled representation through an MLP to produce posterior statistics \((\mu, \sigma^2)\)

Unobserved junctions are left out of the input rather than set to zero, so no values are imputed at the input.

docs.title: Splicing likelihood
docs.text:
Three options are supported.

Option Description binomial Simple binomial over junction read counts beta_binomial Beta-binomial with a learned per-junction concentration \(\phi_j\) dirichlet_multinomial Dirichlet-multinomial over the junctions of each ATSE, with a learned concentration per ATSE, so junction probabilities within an ATSE sum to 1

The default, used for the paper's models, is dirichlet_multinomial.

docs.title: Modality mixing
docs.text:
The two per-modality posteriors are combined into a single joint posterior before sampling. The mixing strategy is controlled by the modality_weights argument. equal, universal and cell are the options of MultiVI.

Option Description equal Fixed 50/50 average (default) universal One global learned weight per modality cell Per-cell learned weights per_dimension_weighted_average One learned splicing weight per latent dimension, with mean weight 0.5 concatenate Concatenate both latents (no mixing, doubled latent size)

docs.text: Component Default Options Splicing encoder partial vanilla, partial Splicing decoder vanilla vanilla, linear Expression decoder vanilla vanilla, linear Splicing likelihood dirichlet_multinomial binomial, beta_binomial, dirichlet_multinomial Latent distribution normal normal, ln

docs.title: splicevi.SPLICEVI
docs.text:
Bases: VAEMixin, UnsupervisedTrainingMixin, BaseModelClass, ArchesMixin

Joint model of gene expression and alternative splicing (junction usage) in single cells.

SPLICEVI learns one latent space from both modalities: an expression encoder and a splicing encoder each give a posterior over the latent space, the two are mixed into a joint posterior, and one decoder per modality reconstructs the data (zero-inflated negative binomial for expression, Dirichlet-multinomial over the junctions of each ATSE for splicing). It wraps the :class:~splicevi.splicevae.SPLICEVAE module.

The defaults are the settings of the paper's models, so SPLICEVI(mdata) followed by model.train() trains the paper's model. :meth:preset returns the same settings as dictionaries, with the variants for a batch key (atlas="tms") and for a reference plus a sparse atlas ("sparse", joint=True).

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default adata AnnOrMuData

MuData object with the modalities "rna" and "splicing", registered with :meth:setup_mudata.

required n_genes int | None

Number of genes. Taken from the registered data when left as None.

None n_junctions int | None

Number of junctions. Taken from the registered data when left as None.

None modality_weights Literal['equal', 'cell', 'universal', 'concatenate', 'per_dimension_weighted_average']

How the two posteriors are mixed into the joint latent:

  • "equal" (default): equal weight per modality,
  • "universal": one learned weight per modality,
  • "cell": learned weights per cell,
  • "concatenate": no mixing; the two latents are concatenated,
  • "per_dimension_weighted_average": one learned splicing weight per latent dimension (expression weight = 1 - splicing weight), constrained so that the mean weight stays at 0.5.
'equal' modality_penalty Literal['Jeffreys', 'MMD', 'None']

Penalty that aligns the two posteriors: "None" (default), "Jeffreys" or "MMD".

'None' n_hidden int | None

Width of the hidden layers of the encoders and decoders. If None (default), the square root of the number of junctions, capped at 128.

None n_latent int | None

Dimension of the latent space (of each modality's latent before concatenation). Default 30. If None, the square root of n_hidden.

30 n_layers_encoder int

Hidden layers in the encoders, including the network after pooling in the partial splicing encoder. Default 2.

2 n_layers_decoder int

Hidden layers in the decoders (not used by the linear decoders). Default 2.

2 dropout_rate float

Dropout rate in the hidden layers. Default 0.01.

0.01 use_batch_norm Literal['encoder', 'decoder', 'none', 'both']

Where to apply batch normalization: "encoder", "decoder", "both" or "none" (default).

'none' use_layer_norm Literal['encoder', 'decoder', 'none', 'both']

Where to apply layer normalization: "encoder", "decoder", "both" (default) or "none".

'both' latent_distribution Literal['normal', 'ln']

Latent distribution: "normal" (default) or "ln" (logistic normal).

'normal' deeply_inject_covariates bool

If True, covariates enter every decoder layer. Default False.

False encode_covariates bool

If True, covariates are also given to the encoders. Default False.

False gene_likelihood Literal['zinb', 'nb', 'poisson']

Expression likelihood: "zinb" (default), "nb" or "poisson".

'zinb' dispersion Literal['gene', 'gene-batch', 'gene-label', 'gene-cell']

Expression dispersion: "gene" (default), "gene-batch", "gene-label" or "gene-cell".

'gene' fully_paired bool

If True, the model exposes only the joint latent (no latent per modality). Default False.

False **model_kwargs

Passed on to :class:~splicevi.splicevae.SPLICEVAE.

{}

Other Parameters:

Name Type Description variance_mixing Literal['sqrt_weights', 'linear', 'squared']

How the two encoders' variances are combined into the joint posterior variance (every modality_weights except "concatenate"; the joint mean is always the weighted average of the two means):

  • "squared" (default): sum(w**2 * v), the variance of a weighted average of independent Gaussians,
  • "sqrt_weights": for equal/cell/universal weights the MultiVI rule sum(sqrt(w) * v) (about 1.41 times the average variance under equal weights); for per_dimension_weighted_average (sum(w * std))**2,
  • "linear": sum(w * v).
mask_cells_without_splicing bool

If True, cells with no observed junction get no splicing weight in the joint latent and are left out of the alignment penalty. Default False: every cell counts as having splicing.

splicing_loss_type Literal['binomial', 'beta_binomial', 'dirichlet_multinomial']

Splicing likelihood: "dirichlet_multinomial" (default), "beta_binomial" or "binomial".

dm_concentration Literal['atse', 'scalar']

Dirichlet-multinomial concentration: "atse" (default; one learned concentration per ATSE) or "scalar" (one shared value).

splicing_loss_weight float

Multiplier of the splicing reconstruction loss relative to the expression reconstruction loss. Default 1.0.

lambda_prior float

Weight of the L2 penalty that pulls each learned log-concentration toward 0 (phi_prior="l2_log" only). Default 0.01; 0.0 turns it off.

phi_floor float

Minimum concentration: phi = phi_floor + softplus(log_phi). Default 0.0.

phi_prior Literal['l2_log', 'gamma', 'none']

Regularizer on the concentration: "l2_log" (default; see lambda_prior), "gamma" (Gamma prior on phi with phi_prior_shape and phi_prior_rate, scaled by 1 / number of cells) or "none".

phi_prior_shape float

Shape and rate of the Gamma prior. Defaults 2.0 and 0.1 (mean 20).

phi_prior_rate float

Shape and rate of the Gamma prior. Defaults 2.0 and 0.1 (mean 20).

phi_init Literal['log100', 'prior', 'constant']

Starting concentration: "constant" (default; every ATSE starts at the same value, phi about 4.6), "log100" (the same start plus a random draw per ATSE) or "prior" (a draw from the Gamma prior).

psi_prior_pseudocount float

Strength of the pseudo-count term on the decoded junction usage: adds -psi_prior_pseudocount * sum_j pop_psi_j * log(psi_j) per cell, i.e. that many virtual reads per ATSE distributed as the read-weighted population usage of the training data. Dirichlet-multinomial only. Default 0.0 (off).

splicing_encoder_architecture Literal['vanilla', 'partial']

Splicing encoder: "partial" (default; reads only the observed junctions of each cell) or "vanilla" (scvi-tools Encoder on the full junction vector).

splicing_decoder_architecture Literal['vanilla', 'linear']

Splicing decoder: "vanilla" (default; nonlinear) or "linear".

expression_architecture Literal['vanilla', 'linear']

Expression decoder: "vanilla" (default; nonlinear) or "linear".

encoder_hidden_dim int

Width of the network after pooling in the partial splicing encoder. Default 128.

code_dim int

Size of the learned embedding of each junction in the partial splicing encoder. Default 64.

h_hidden_dim int

Width of the network that combines each observed junction's input with its embedding. Default 128.

pool_mode Literal['mean', 'sum']

Pooling over the observed junctions of a cell: "mean" (default) or "sum".

psi_input Literal['raw', 'deviation']

Input of the partial splicing encoder: "deviation" (default; each observed junction's usage minus its read-weighted population usage, pooled with a fixed divisor so the pooled code does not carry the number of observed junctions; needs pool_mode="mean") or "raw" (the observed usage itself).

decoder_intercept_init Literal['default', 'population']

Starting bias of the splicing decoder: "population" (default; set so that the decoder starts at the read-weighted population usage of the training data) or "default" (PyTorch's initialization).

decoder_depth_covariates bool

If True (default), both decoders (never the encoders) receive three standardized depth inputs per cell: log1p detected genes, log1p observed junctions and log1p library size. Vanilla splicing decoder only.

max_nobs int

Largest number of observed (cell, junction) pairs processed in one chunk by the partial encoder; a negative value (default -1) processes a batch in one chunk.

n_decoder_covariates int

Number of zero-initialized covariate inputs into the first hidden layer of both decoders. Default 0. Normally left at 0 and added by :meth:finetune_decoders (one input, technology); a saved fine-tuned model stores it, so :meth:load rebuilds the inputs. Vanilla decoders only.

initialize_embeddings_from_pca bool

If True (default) and the splicing encoder is "partial", the junction embeddings start from a truncated SVD of the junction usage matrix.

Examples:

>>> SPLICEVI.setup_mudata(mdata)   # the paper's layer names; add batch_key if there is one
>>> model = SPLICEVI(mdata)
>>> model.train()
>>> latent = model.get_latent_representation()

  • "zinb_expected" (default): the ZINB expected expression (1 - dropout) * px_scale. With ZINB the dropout probability can absorb part of a difference between groups, which px_scale alone then misses (on Allen Brain data downsampled to EasySci depth this roughly doubled the fold changes towards the full-depth ones). For a model with gene_likelihood="nb" or "poisson" there is no dropout, so this is the decoder output.
  • "decoder": the decoder output px_scale (:meth:get_normalized_expression), as in scVI and MultiVI.

docs.title: finetune_decoders(query_mdata, reference_mdata, n_query_per_step=32, n_reference_per_step=128, lr=0.0001, max_epochs=300, early_stopping_patience=30, validation_fraction=0.1, seed=20261137, set_torch_seed=True, max_minutes=None, checkpoint_dir=None, fix_depth_inputs=True, query_covariate_value=1.0, reference_covariate_value=0.0)
docs.text:
Adapt a trained model to a new atlas by fine-tuning only its decoders, plus one technology input.

Use when this model was trained on a reference atlas (e.g. Allen Brain, deep Smart-seq) and you want its expression and splicing estimates for a new, sparser atlas of the same tissue (e.g. EasySci, single-nucleus 3') without retraining from scratch. The encoders are not changed, so query cells are placed in the reference latent space; the decoders learn the query data's expression and splicing levels. Defaults are the same as what's used in the paper's EasySci model.

What happens:

  1. One zero-initialized decoder covariate input is added to the first hidden layer of both decoders (technology: reference_covariate_value for reference cells, query_covariate_value for query cells). At zero weights the model is the reference model.
  2. Everything is frozen except the two decoders and the covariate weights. Kept from the reference model: the encoders, junction embeddings and latent mixing, the deviation input's population PSI and pool divisor, the per-ATSE splicing concentrations and the gene dispersions (re-learning the last two on the query data predicted held-out query reads worse in the paper's tests, so it is not offered).
  3. With fix_depth_inputs (models with decoder_depth_covariates), the decoders' depth inputs are fixed at the reference training mean for every cell, since the reference depth statistics do not describe the query data. The cross-modality gate is set open, as at the end of training.
  4. Each step uses n_query_per_step query cells and n_reference_per_step reference cells (the reference "replay" keeps the decoders fitting the reference); loss = query loss + reference loss; Adam at lr.
  5. A random validation_fraction of the query cells is held out for early stopping (patience early_stopping_patience epochs, at most max_epochs, optional wall-clock limit max_minutes).
  6. The best state is restored and the model is left decoding as query data (decoder covariate = query_covariate_value), ready for :meth:differential_splicing etc. on the query cells.

Calling it again continues from the current weights with a fresh optimizer. Training a fine-tuned model with :meth:train is not supported: every cell would get decoder_covariate_value, so the covariate weights would act as a plain bias.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default query_mdata MuData

The new atlas (e.g. EasySci training metacells) in this model's gene and junction space (same genes, same junction ids and ATSE assignment), with the layers this model was trained on: expression counts (length_norm; raw counts for UMI data), library size (X_library_size), junction and ATSE counts, junc_ratio and psi_mask. If not yet set up, it is set up with this model's setup arguments (as :meth:load does). The paper's reproduction code (SpliceVI-utils) shows how these files were built from the model-ready data.

required reference_mdata MuData

A replay set of the data this model was trained on (e.g. 20,000 Allen training cells), same layers.

required n_query_per_step int

Query and reference cells per optimization step (paper: 32 and 128).

32 n_reference_per_step int

Query and reference cells per optimization step (paper: 32 and 128).

32 lr float

Adam learning rate.

0.0001 max_epochs int

Epochs over the query training cells; stop when the validation loss has not improved for this many epochs.

300 early_stopping_patience int

Epochs over the query training cells; stop when the validation loss has not improved for this many epochs.

300 validation_fraction float

Share of query cells held out (never trained on) to decide when to stop.

0.1 seed int

Seed of the validation split, the minibatch order and the reference cells per step (numpy), and, with set_torch_seed, of torch's global random state (latent sampling and decoder dropout during fine-tuning). GPU arithmetic is not bit-deterministic, so reruns agree closely but not exactly.

20261137 set_torch_seed bool

Call torch.manual_seed(seed) (changes torch's global random state). False when the caller seeded torch already, e.g. before loading the model, as the paper's fine-tuning run did.

True max_minutes float | None

Optional wall-clock limit (the best state so far is kept). Keep it below a job's time limit.

None checkpoint_dir str | None

If set, the best module state is also written to <checkpoint_dir>/module_state_best.pt at every improvement, so a run killed from outside (e.g. a job time limit) keeps its best state.

None fix_depth_inputs bool

Fix the decoders' depth inputs at the reference training mean (models with decoder depth covariates).

True query_covariate_value float

Values of the technology input for query and reference cells.

1.0 reference_covariate_value float

Values of the technology input for query and reference cells.

1.0

Returns:

Type Description Training history: one row per epoch (``epoch``, ``train_loss``, ``validation_loss``; epoch -1 = before training). Also stored as ``finetune_history_``, with the settings and outcome in ``finetune_params_``; both are saved by :meth:`save`.

Examples:

>>> model = SPLICEVI.load(reference_model_dir, adata=query_mdata)
>>> model.to_device("cuda")
>>> history = model.finetune_decoders(query_mdata, reference_mdata)
>>> model.save(out_dir)                         # SPLICEVI.load(out_dir, adata=query_mdata) decodes as query
>>> ds = model.differential_splicing(adata=query_mdata, groupby="broad_cell_type", group1="A", group2="B")

docs.title: get_normalized_expression_ZINB(adata=None, indices=None, n_samples_overall=None, transform_batch=None, gene_list=None, use_z_mean=True, n_samples=1, batch_size=None, return_mean=True, return_numpy=False, silent=True, sample=False, return_counts=False)
docs.text:
Returns ZINB posterior-mean normalized expression (the expression analogue of :meth:get_normalized_splicing_DM). Only valid for gene_likelihood="zinb".

The ZINB is a Gamma-Poisson mixed with a point mass at zero. With decoder mean :math:\mu (px_rate), inverse dispersion :math:\theta (px_r) and dropout probability :math:\pi = \sigma(\text{px\_dropout}), the posterior mean of the underlying rate given the observed count :math:y is

  • :math:y > 0: :math:E[\lambda \mid y] = \mu (\theta + y) / (\theta + \mu), i.e. a weighted average :math:\tfrac{\theta}{\theta+\mu}\mu + \tfrac{\mu}{\theta+\mu} y of the decoder and the data;
  • :math:y = 0: with :math:w = P(\text{dropout} \mid y=0) = \pi / (\pi + (1-\pi)(\theta/(\theta+\mu))^\theta), :math:E[\lambda \mid 0] = w \mu + (1-w)\, \theta\mu / (\theta+\mu) (a dropout zero carries no information; a sampling zero pulls the estimate down).

The result is divided by the cell's library factor (px_rate / px_scale), so it is on the same scale as :meth:get_normalized_expression (px_scale) and can replace it in DE. Parameters and return shape are the same as :meth:get_normalized_expression, plus:

sample If True, return one random draw from the posterior instead of its mean: for y > 0, :math:\lambda \sim \mathrm{Gamma}(\theta + y,\ \theta/\mu + 1); for y = 0, with probability w the prior :math:\mathrm{Gamma}(\theta, \theta/\mu) (dropout zero) and otherwise :math:\mathrm{Gamma}(\theta, \theta/\mu + 1) (Gamma shape / rate). Used by DE with norm_expression_function="zinb_posterior_sample", so each Monte Carlo draw carries the uncertainty of each cell's expression given its counts. return_counts If True, do not divide by the library factor (values on the count scale, e.g. for pseudobulk sums).

docs.text:
Returns DM-normalized splicing probabilities (PSI*).

This decodes junction PSI (:math:p) and applies a Dirichlet–multinomial posterior mean smoothing per junction: :math:\psi^\* = (c p + y_j) / (c + n), where :math:y_j is the observed junction count and :math:n is the observed ATSE total for that junction. The concentration :math:c is taken from the module: * If self.dm_concentration == "atse": use the per-ATSE values in self.module.log_phi_j mapped to per-junction via self.module.junc2atse. * Otherwise: treat self.module.log_phi_j as a scalar concentration.

Optional subset of junction names to return.

>>> SPLICEVI.setup_mudata(mdata, rna_layer="raw_counts")  # expression counts in another layer

docs.title: Differential Expression & Splicing
docs.text:
SpliceVI supports both differential gene expression (DE) and differential splicing (DS) analysis between groups of cells. Both use the same underlying Bayesian framework from scvi-tools and differ only in what quantity is being compared and how the effect size is defined. The API mirrors MultiVI, with differential_splicing and get_normalized_splicing replacing the chromatin accessibility equivalents.

For full background on the statistical framework, see the scvi-tools differential expression guide.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
Both DE and DS use _de_core from scvi-tools internally, in three steps.

  1. Sample normalized values from the posterior for each cell in group 1 and group 2 separately, by passing cells through the encoder and then the relevant decoder (expression or splicing)
  2. Compute a per-feature effect size from those posterior samples
  3. Estimate the posterior probability that the effect size is at least \(\delta\) in one direction (the "change" mode)

Each feature is scored by the larger of the two one-sided probabilities, and its log Bayes factor follows from it,

\[ p = \max\{P(\Delta \geq \delta \mid \text{data}),\ P(\Delta \leq -\delta \mid \text{data})\}, \qquad \text{BF} = \log \frac{p}{1 - p} \]

Features are called at a posterior expected false discovery rate (default 5%). The calls are the largest set of features, taken in order of decreasing \(p\), whose mean \(1 - p\) is at most that rate.

docs.title: Differential Expression
docs.text:
DE compares normalized gene expression between two groups. By default (norm_expression_function="zinb_expected") this is the ZINB expected expression, (1 − dropout probability) × the decoder output (get_normalized_expression(expected=True), see Imputed Splicing & Expression). With a ZINB likelihood the dropout probability can absorb part of a difference between groups, which the decoder output alone then misses. norm_expression_function="decoder" compares the decoder output, as scVI and MultiVI do, and "zinb_posterior_mean" and "zinb_posterior_sample" use each cell's ZINB posterior given its observed counts.

The effect size follows the standard scVI convention, a log-fold change,

\[ \text{LFC} = \log_2(\hat{x}^{(2)}_g + \epsilon) - \log_2(\hat{x}^{(1)}_g + \epsilon) \]

where \(\hat{x}^{(k)}_g\) is the posterior mean normalized expression for gene \(g\) in group \(k\).

de_results = model.differential_expression(
    adata=mdata,
    groupby="cell_type",
    group1="Neuron",
    group2="Astrocyte",
    delta=0.25,
    fdr_target=0.05,
    norm_expression_function="zinb_expected",   # the default
)

docs.title: Differential Splicing
docs.text:
DS compares junction usage (PSI) between two groups. Because PSI is already on a \([0, 1]\) probability scale, the effect size is a direct difference rather than a log-fold change, as for ATAC-seq accessibility scores in scvi-tools,

\[ \text{effect size} = \hat{\psi}^{(2)}_j - \hat{\psi}^{(1)}_j \]

where \(\hat{\psi}^{(k)}_j\) is the PSI for junction \(j\) in group \(k\). By default (norm_splicing_function="dm_posterior_sample") each Monte Carlo sample draws every cell's PSI from its DM posterior, so per-cell read uncertainty enters proba_ds. norm_splicing_function="dm_posterior_mean" uses the posterior mean instead, and norm_splicing_function="decoder" the decoder output alone.

ds_results = model.differential_splicing(
    adata=mdata,
    groupby="cell_type",
    group1="Neuron",
    group2="Astrocyte",
    delta=0.10,
    fdr_target=0.05,
    norm_splicing_function="dm_posterior_sample",   # the default
)

docs.title: Output columns
docs.text: Column Description proba_ds Posterior probability of differential splicing is_ds_fdr Boolean FDR-controlled call at fdr_target bayes_factor Log Bayes factor effect_size \(\hat{\psi}^{(2)} - \hat{\psi}^{(1)}\) (model posterior means) emp_effect Empirical \(\bar{\psi}^{(2)} - \bar{\psi}^{(1)}\) from observed PSI values est_prob1 / est_prob2 Model posterior mean PSI per group emp_prob1 / emp_prob2 Empirical mean PSI per group (observed cells only) n_obs_group1 / n_obs_group2 Number of cells with observed data per junction per group

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• The paper keeps a differential splicing call only when its ATSE has reads in at least three cells (or metacells) of each group. Apply this with splicevi.filter_read_support(ds_results, min_units=3), which does not change the FDR calls themselves
  • Both methods support batch_correction=True to marginalize over batch effects when comparing groups
  • proba_ds / proba_de are Monte Carlo estimates. Pass seed= (for example seed=0) to get the same table on repeated calls
  • Features with equal posterior probability keep their order in the data, both in the row order of the DE table and in which of them are called when they are tied at the FDR cutoff, so the calls are the same on every machine

docs.title: Imputed Splicing & Expression
docs.text: A trained model can be applied to other cells with the same genes and junctions as the training data, such as held-out test cells, without retraining. The model's learned parameters stay fixed. For data from a different protocol, the paper first fine-tunes the model's decoders on the new data (finetune_decoders).

docs.title: Normalized expression
docs.text:
get_normalized_expression returns the decoder-predicted normalized expression for each gene, analogous to scVI's \(\rho_n\). This is the per-gene fraction of total expression predicted by the model, averaged over posterior samples if requested.

expr = model.get_normalized_expression(
    adata=mdata,          # can be held-out data not seen during training
    n_samples=25,
    return_mean=True,
)
# returns DataFrame of shape (cells × genes)

With the default zero-inflated negative binomial likelihood, expected=True returns the expected expression instead, \((1 - \pi_{ng})\,\rho_{ng}\) with \(\pi_{ng}\) the decoder's dropout probability. Differential expression compares this quantity by default (norm_expression_function="zinb_expected").

docs.title: Normalized splicing (decoder output)
docs.text:
get_normalized_splicing returns the raw decoder-predicted PSI (\(p_{nj}\)) for each junction, the model's prediction based solely on the latent representation, before any smoothing toward observed counts.

psi = model.get_normalized_splicing(
    adata=mdata,
    n_samples=25,
    return_mean=True,
)
# returns DataFrame of shape (cells × junctions)

docs.title: DM-normalized splicing (posterior mean PSI)
docs.text:
get_normalized_splicing_DM returns a Dirichlet-Multinomial posterior mean estimate of PSI that blends the decoder prediction with the cell's own observed junction counts,

\[ \psi^*_j = \frac{c \cdot p_j + y_j}{c + n_j} \]

where

  • \(p_j\) is the decoder-predicted PSI for junction \(j\)
  • \(y_j\) is the observed junction read count for that cell
  • \(n_j\) is the observed total read count of that junction's ATSE
  • \(c\) is the learned concentration of the junction's ATSE (one per ATSE by default, or one shared value with dm_concentration="scalar")

This gives data-adaptive shrinkage. Cells with high read coverage are pulled toward their own observations, and cells with low coverage rely more on the decoder's prediction. When dm_concentration="atse", \(c\) is a per-ATSE value, so the shrinkage differs between ATSEs.

psi_dm = model.get_normalized_splicing_DM(
    adata=mdata,
    n_samples=25,
    return_mean=True,
)
# returns DataFrame of shape (cells × junctions)

differential_splicing uses the same posterior. By default it draws one sample from it per Monte Carlo sample (norm_splicing_function="dm_posterior_sample"), and norm_splicing_function="dm_posterior_mean" uses this mean (see Differential Expression & Splicing).

docs.title: Latent Space
docs.text:
After training, SpliceVI exposes three latent representations.

Method Description get_latent_representation() Joint latent \(z\), mixed from both modalities get_latent_representation(modality="expression") Expression-only posterior mean \(\mu_e\) get_latent_representation(modality="splicing") Splicing-only posterior mean \(\mu_s\)

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
# Joint latent (default)
z = model.get_latent_representation(adata=mdata)   # (cells × n_latent)

# Modality-specific
z_expr = model.get_latent_representation(adata=mdata, modality="expression")
z_spl  = model.get_latent_representation(adata=mdata, modality="splicing")

The joint latent can be used with standard tools such as scanpy, for example to draw a UMAP.

import scanpy as sc

rna = mdata["rna"]                      # scanpy works on AnnData objects
rna.obsm["X_splicevi"] = z
sc.pp.neighbors(rna, use_rep="X_splicevi")
sc.tl.umap(rna)
sc.pl.umap(rna, color="cell_type")

docs.title: Imputed PSI values
docs.text:
The model also gives imputed junction usage (PSI) for every cell and junction.

psi = model.get_normalized_splicing_DM()   # (cells × junctions), posterior mean given the cell's reads
psi_decoder = model.get_normalized_splicing()   # the decoder's prediction from the latent alone

get_normalized_splicing_DM combines the decoder's prediction with the cell's own reads, and is the estimate differential splicing uses by default. See Imputed Splicing & Expression for both.
